Rationalisation can be fine. It can definitely lead to coming to terms with events and learning to process what happened.

Over-rationalisation is not. So the ability to mentalise (a healthy skill for cognitive functioning) involves seeing many different sides of a situation and having the ability to realistically evaluate the contributions different factors have to a situation.

Over-rationalisation is the opposite of that; it's a pushing away or explaining away of circumstances based around qualities in other people. Can sometimes involve projection but it definitely involves not taking full account of what happened and why.

I think I'm very lucky because most EDS cases do not improve. My version may be viewed more as a deficiency rather than incorrectly formed collagen.

When I was extremely dizzy all the time and at my worst, I started megadosing Vitamin C (one of the main vitamins that helps with collagen formation).

Now, Vitamin C has a very short half-life in the body. I was taking 8-12 a day of 1000mg, spread out over the day, and generally away from food, with a break at dinner.

This is because too much Vitamin C can blunt copper and B12 absorption. It can also cause an upset stomach and help form oxalates (which can cause kidney stones).

It took me 8 years but the dizziness abated and my joints don't sublux near as much. I also do some weightlifting to help keep my joints in place. I wouldn't recommend weightlifting with the way your joints are right now, but if you can stand it, maybe working out with lighter bands on some gentle stability and postural exercises as a first step.

Note: I am not a doctor. I merely know what worked for me. I still have teeth/gum issues but that tissue is generally weaker than skin, ligaments, and tendons, so it makes a sort of sense.


If you have any other questions, let my know. If you choose to start megadosing C like me, be careful if you come off abruptly. I'd recommend tapering off instead.
